    n=$(grep -c "^\." "$f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)

`grep -c` prints its count (including `0`) AND exits non-zero when the count is zero, so the `|| echo 0` fires as well and `n` ends up as `"0\n0"`. That corrupts the status line the operator reads.     n=$(grep -c "^\." "$f" 2>/dev/null)
